372.subject: Botany
372.text: In succulent plants the stomata open in night and close in day. Which among the following would be best hypothesis to explain the mechanism of stomatal action in night only?
options: \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) accumulates, reduces \(\mathrm{pH}\), stimulate enzymes resulting in accumulation of sugars.
Increase in \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) concentration, conversion of organic acids into starch resulting in the increased conversion into sugars resulting in \(\mathrm{K}^{+}\)transport.
Low \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) concentration accumulates organic acids resulting in the increased concentration of cell sap.
\(\mathrm{CO}_2\) used up, increase \(\mathrm{pH}\) results in accumulation of sugars.
372.sol:
In CAM plants stomata open at night. In these plants night acidification occurs. i.e., malic acid is synthesised during night due to incomplete oxidation of carbohydrates.
In night, $2 \mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_{12} \mathrm{O}_6+3 \mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow 3 \mathrm{C}_4 \mathrm{H}_6 \mathrm{O}_5+3 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ (malic acid)
$\downarrow$ leads to opening of stomata At night malic acid formed in guard cells dissociates into $\mathrm{H}^{+}$and malate ions. $\mathrm{K}^{+}$ion exchange from subsidiary cells with $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ions. Thus due to accumulation of $\mathrm{K}^{+}$ions osmotic pressure of guard cells increases, endosmosis occurs anDguard cells become turgid due to which stomata opens. The malic acid at day time breaks into $\mathrm{CO}_2$ and pyruvic acid thus increasing the concentration of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ in mesophyll cells. This is utilised in Calvin cycle to form sugar which is finally converted into starch.

Alcohols have the molecular formula as ${C}_{n}{H}_{2n + 2}O$. They do not have any unsaturation. The carboxylic acids have the unsaturation with two oxygen atoms. Ether does not have the unsaturation with one oxygen. Ethers also have the unsaturation with two oxygen atoms. Aldehydes have the unsaturation with one oxygen.

Hence, alcohols with molecular formula ${C}_{n}{H}_{2n + 2}O$ are isomeric with ethers.

19602.subject: Chemistry
19602.text: Which of the following amines cannot be prepared by Gabriel's phthalimide synthesis?
19602.sol:
Gabriel phthalimide synthesis involves the reaction of potassium phthalimide with an alkyl halide to form an N-alkyl phthalimide, which is subsequently hydrolyzed to yield a primary amine.

The reaction proceeds via an $S_N2$ mechanism. Therefore, the alkyl halide used must be a primary or secondary alkyl halide. Tertiary alkyl halides undergo elimination reactions instead of substitution, and aryl halides do not undergo $S_N2$ reactions with the phthalimide anion.

Analyzing the options:
1. 2-phenylethylamine is a primary amine and can be prepared from 2-phenylethyl chloride.
2. n-propylamine is a primary amine and can be prepared from n-propyl chloride.
3. N-methylbenzylamine is a secondary amine. Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is specifically used for the preparation of primary amines only. It cannot be used to prepare secondary or tertiary amines because the phthalimide anion is a bulky nucleophile and the resulting N-alkyl phthalimide does not allow for further alkylation to form secondary amines.
4. Isobutyl amine is a primary amine and can be prepared from isobutyl chloride.

Thus, N-methylbenzylamine cannot be prepared by this method.

Answer: N-methylbenzylamine

The complex $\left[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{ox})_3\right]^{3-}$ is a tris-chelated complex of the form $M(AA)_3$. It exhibits optical isomerism but does not show geometrical isomerism because all donor atoms are identical.

The complex $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{3-}$ is an octahedral complex of the form $MA_6$. It does not exhibit either geometrical or optical isomerism.

The complex $\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_2 \mathrm{Cl}_2\right]^{+}$ is of the form $M(AA)_2 a_2$. The cis-isomer of this complex is optically active (chiral) and also exists as a geometrical isomer (cis and trans). The trans-isomer is optically inactive due to the presence of a plane of symmetry. Since the cis-isomer exhibits both geometrical (relative to trans) and optical isomerism, this complex satisfies the condition.

The complex $\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NO}_3)_3(\mathrm{NH}_3)_3\right]$ is of the form $Ma_3b_3$. It exhibits geometrical isomerism (fac and mer isomers) but does not exhibit optical isomerism as both isomers possess planes of symmetry.

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{en})_2 \mathrm{Cl}_2\right]^{+}$

20421.subject: Chemistry
20421.text: Coupling reaction is an example of
20421.sol:
Coupling reactions, such as the formation of azo dyes from diazonium salts and aromatic compounds (like phenols or amines), involve the attack of a diazonium cation on an electron-rich aromatic ring.

The diazonium cation, $Ar-N_{2}^{+}$, acts as a weak electrophile. It attacks the electron-rich aromatic ring, which acts as a nucleophile.

This process results in the replacement of a hydrogen atom on the aromatic ring by the diazonium group, which is a characteristic feature of electrophilic aromatic substitution.

Therefore, the coupling reaction is classified as an electrophilic substitution reaction.

Answer: electrophilic substitution reaction.

20623.subject: Chemistry
20623.text: What is the percentage dissociation of 0.8ml of Acetic acid (density is 1.04g/ml) which is dissolved in 1.2L of water if the observed Depression in freezing point is 0.0228 K? (K_f$ for water = 1.86Kkg/mol.)$
20623.sol:
Mass of acetic acid $= \text{Volume} \times \text{Density} = 0.8 \times 1.04 = 0.832 \text{ g}$

Molar mass of acetic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$) $= 60 \text{ g/mol}$

Number of moles of acetic acid $= \dfrac{0.832}{60} = 0.01387 \text{ mol}$

Mass of water $= 1.2 \text{ L} \times 1 \text{ kg/L} = 1.2 \text{ kg}$

Molality ($m$) $= \dfrac{\text{Moles of solute}}{\text{Mass of solvent in kg}} = \dfrac{0.01387}{1.2} = 0.01156 \text{ mol/kg}$

Theoretical depression in freezing point ($\Delta T_{f(\text{th})}$) $= K_f \times m = 1.86 \times 0.01156 = 0.0215 \text{ K}$

Observed depression in freezing point ($\Delta T_f$) $= 0.0228 \text{ K}$

van't Hoff factor ($i$) $= \dfrac{\text{Observed } \Delta T_f}{\text{Theoretical } \Delta T_{f(\text{th})}} = \dfrac{0.0228}{0.0215} \approx 1.06$

For the dissociation of acetic acid:
$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_3\text{COO}^- + \text{H}^+$

$i = 1 + \alpha$

$1.06 = 1 + \alpha \Rightarrow \alpha = 0.06$

Percentage dissociation $= \alpha \times 100 = 0.06 \times 100 = 6\%$

Answer: $6$

21097.subject: Mathematics
21097.text: In the expansion of $\left(1-3 x+3 x^2-x^3\right)^{2 n}$, the middle term is
21097.sol:
The given expression is $\left(1-3x+3x^2-x^3\right)^{2n}$.

Observe that $1-3x+3x^2-x^3 = (1-x)^3$.

Substituting this into the expression, we get $\left((1-x)^3\right)^{2n} = (1-x)^{6n}$.

The expansion of $(1-x)^{6n}$ has $6n+1$ terms.

The middle term of an expansion with $N$ terms is the $\left(\dfrac{N+1}{2}\right)$ th term.

Here, $N = 6n+1$, so the middle term is the $\left(\dfrac{6n+1+1}{2}\right)$ th term = $\left(\dfrac{6n+2}{2}\right)$ th term = $(3n+1)$ th term.

Answer: $(3 n+1)$ th term

Let $I = \int_{-\pi / 2}^{\pi / 2} \sin x \, dx$.

The integrand $f(x) = \sin x$ is an odd function because $f(-x) = \sin(-x) = -\sin x = -f(x)$.

For any odd function $f(x)$ integrated over a symmetric interval $[-a, a]$, the integral is zero:

Therefore, $\int_{-\pi / 2}^{\pi / 2} \sin x \, dx = 0$.

22380.subject: Physics
22380.text: A coil offers a resistance of $20 \mathrm{ ohm}$ for a direct current. If we send an alternating current through the same coil, the resistance offered by the coil to the alternating current will be :
22380.sol:
A coil is characterized by its resistance $R$ and its self-inductance $L$. When a direct current (DC) flows through the coil, the frequency $f$ is $0$, so the inductive reactance $X_L = 2\pi f L = 0$. Thus, the total impedance $Z$ for DC is equal to the resistance $R = 20 \Omega$.

When an alternating current (AC) flows through the coil, the frequency $f > 0$, which results in an inductive reactance $X_L = 2\pi f L > 0$. The impedance $Z$ for AC is given by $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_L^2}$.

Since $X_L > 0$, it follows that $Z = \sqrt{20^2 + X_L^2} > \sqrt{20^2} = 20 \Omega$. Therefore, the coil offers a greater resistance (impedance) to the alternating current compared to the direct current.

Answer: Greater than $20 \Omega$

23440.subject: Physics
23440.text: A solid cylinder of mass $2 \mathrm{ kg}$ and radius $0.2 \mathrm{ m}$ is rotating about its own axis without friction with angular velocity $5 \mathrm{ rad} \mathrms^{-1}$. A particle of mass $1 \mathrm{ kg}$ moving with a velocity of $5 \mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$ strikes the cylinder and sticks to it as shown in figure. The angular velocity of the system after the particle sticks to it will be
23440.sol:
The initial angular momentum of the system about the axis of rotation is the sum of the angular momentum of the cylinder and the angular momentum of the particle. The cylinder is rotating about its own axis, so its angular momentum is $L_{cyl} = I \omega = (\dfrac{1}{2} M R^2) \omega$.

Given $M = 2 \text{ kg}$, $R = 0.2 \text{ m}$, and $\omega = 5 \text{ rad s}^{-1}$, we have $I = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times (0.2)^2 = 0.04 \text{ kg m}^2$. Thus, $L_{cyl} = 0.04 \times 5 = 0.2 \text{ kg m}^2 \texts^{-1}$.

The particle of mass $m = 1 \text{ kg}$ moves with velocity $v = 5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ at a perpendicular distance $R = 0.2 \text{ m}$ from the axis. Its angular momentum is $L_{part} = m v R = 1 \times 5 \times 0.2 = 1.0 \text{ kg m}^2 \texts^{-1}$.

The total initial angular momentum is $L_{initial} = L_{cyl} + L_{part} = 0.2 + 1.0 = 1.2 \text{ kg m}^2 \texts^{-1}$.

After the particle sticks to the cylinder, the new moment of inertia is $I' = I + m R^2 = 0.04 + 1 \times (0.2)^2 = 0.04 + 0.04 = 0.08 \text{ kg m}^2$.

By conservation of angular momentum, $L_{initial} = L_{final} = I' \omega'$.

$1.2 = 0.08 \times \omega'$.

$\omega' = \dfrac{1.2}{0.08} = \dfrac{120}{8} = 15.0 \text{ rad s}^{-1}$.

Answer: $15.0 \mathrm{ rad s}^{-1}$

23444.subject: Physics
23444.text: A thin circular ring of mass ,$M$ and radius $R$ rotates about an axis through its centre and perpendicular to its plane, with a constant angular velocity $\omega$. Four small spheres each of mass $m$ (negligible radius) are kept gently to the opposite ends of two mutually perpendicular diameters of the ring. The new angular velocity of the ring will be
23444.sol:
The initial moment of inertia of the ring about the axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its plane is $I_1 = MR^2$.

The initial angular momentum of the system is $L = I_1 \omega = MR^2 \omega$.

When four small spheres of mass $m$ are placed at the ends of two mutually perpendicular diameters, they are at a distance $R$ from the axis of rotation. The new moment of inertia of the system becomes $I_2 = MR^2 + 4(mR^2) = (M + 4m)R^2$.

Since no external torque acts on the system, the angular momentum is conserved, so $L_1 = L_2$.

$MR^2 \omega = (M + 4m)R^2 \omega'$, where $\omega'$ is the new angular velocity.

Solving for $\omega'$, we get $\omega' = \dfrac{MR^2 \omega}{(M + 4m)R^2} = \left( \dfrac{M}{M + 4m} \right) \omega$.

Answer: $\left(\dfrac{M}{M+4 m}\right) \omega$

23630.subject: Physics
23630.text: If the intensity of the central maximum in the Young's double slit experiment is $I_0$, what will be the intensity at the same region when one of the slits is blocked by an opaque object?
23630.sol:
Let the intensity of light from each slit be $I$.

The intensity of the central maximum in Young's double slit experiment is given by $I_\max = (\sqrt{I} + \sqrt{I})^2 = 4I$.

Given that $I_\max = I_0$, we have $I_0 = 4I \Rightarrow I = \dfrac{I_0}{4}$.

When one of the slits is blocked, there is no interference. The intensity at any point on the screen is solely due to the light from the single unblocked slit.

Thus, the intensity at the same region will be $I = \dfrac{I_0}{4}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{I_0}{4}$

24966.subject: Chemistry
24966.text:
Passage: Consider the following reaction sequence in which $\textbf{J}$, $\textbf{K}$, $\textbf{L}$ and $\textbf{M}$ are the major products.

Given:
Atomic mass (in amu): H : $1$, C : $12$, N : $14$, O : $16$, S : $32$, Br : $80$, Ba : $137$

Question: In sulphur estimation by Carius method, the amount of BaSO$_4$ formed from $3.79$ g of $\textbf{M}$ is ____ g.
24966.sol:
Step 1: The starting material is $m$-xylene (1,3-dimethylbenzene). It undergoes Friedel-Crafts acylation with chloroacetyl chloride ($\text{ClCH}_2\text{COCl}$) in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form 2-chloro-1-(2,4-dimethylphenyl)ethanone.

Step 2: The chloro ketone reacts with $\text{NaI}$ (Finkelstein reaction) to form 2-iodo-1-(2,4-dimethylphenyl)ethanone.

Step 3: This iodo compound undergoes Williamson ether synthesis with sodium 3-nitrophenoxide to form compound $\textbf{J}$.
The molecular formula of $\textbf{J}$ is $\text{C}_{16}\text{H}_{15}\text{NO}_4$.

Step 4: Compound $\textbf{J}$ is reduced by $\text{NaBH}_4$, which converts the ketone group to a secondary alcohol. Subsequent reaction with $\text{PBr}_3$ replaces the hydroxyl group with a bromine atom, yielding compound $\textbf{K}$.
The molecular formula of $\textbf{K}$ is $\text{C}_{16}\text{H}_{16}\text{BrNO}_3$.
Molar mass of $\textbf{K} = (16 \times 12) + (16 \times 1) + 80 + 14 + (3 \times 16) = 350 \text{ g/mol}$, which matches the given data.

Step 5: Compound $\textbf{K}$ reacts with sodium thiophenoxide ($\text{PhSNa}$) in an $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reaction, replacing the bromide with a phenylthio group ($\text{-SPh}$) to form compound $\textbf{M}$.
The molecular formula of $\textbf{M}$ is $\text{C}_{16}\text{H}_{16}(\text{SC}_6\text{H}_5)\text{NO}_3 \Rightarrow \text{C}_{22}\text{H}_{21}\text{NO}_3\text{S}$.
Molar mass of $\textbf{M} = 350 - 80 (\text{for Br}) + 109 (\text{for SPh}) = 379 \text{ g/mol}$.

Step 6: Calculate the moles of compound $\textbf{M}$ used in the Carius method.
$\text{Moles of } \textbf{M} = \dfrac{3.79 \text{ g}}{379 \text{ g/mol}} = 0.01 \text{ mol}$.

Step 7: Since each molecule of $\textbf{M}$ contains exactly one sulphur atom, the moles of sulphur present is $0.01 \text{ mol}$. In the Carius method, all sulphur is quantitatively converted to barium sulphate ($\text{BaSO}_4$).
$\text{Moles of BaSO}_4 \text{ formed} = 0.01 \text{ mol}$.

Step 8: Calculate the mass of $\text{BaSO}_4$ formed.
Molar mass of $\text{BaSO}_4 = 137 (\text{Ba}) + 32 (\text{S}) + 4 \times 16 (\text{O}) = 233 \text{ g/mol}$.
$\text{Mass of BaSO}_4 = 0.01 \text{ mol} \times 233 \text{ g/mol} = 2.33 \text{ g}$.

Answer: $2.33$

The correct option(s) about entropy (S) is(are)

[$R =$ gas constant, $F =$ Faraday constant, $T =$ Temperature]
options: For the reaction, $M\left(s\right) + 2{H}^{+}\left(aq\right) \to {H}_{2}\left(g\right) + {M}^{2 +}\left(aq\right)$, if $\dfrac{{dE}_{cell}}{dT} = \dfrac{R}{F}$ then the entropy change of the reaction is $R$ (assume that entropy and internal energy changes are temperature independent).

The cell reaction, $Pt\left(s\right) ∣ {H}_{2}\left(g, 1bar\right)\left|{H}^{+}\left(aq, 0 . 01M\right) ‖ {H}^{+}\left(aq, 0 . 1M\right)\right|{H}_{2}\left(g, 1bar\right) ∣ Pt\left(s\right)$ , is an entropy driven process.
For racemization of an optically active compound, $\DeltaS > 0$
25160.sol:
(A) $M\left(s\right) + 2{H}^{+}\left(aq\right) \to {H}_{2}\left(g\right) + {M}^{2 +}\left(aq\right)$

if $\dfrac{{dE}_{cell}}{dT} = \dfrac{R}{F}$

$\DeltaS = nF\dfrac{dE}{dT} = 2F\left(\dfrac{R}{F}\right) = 2R$

(B) ${E}_{cell} = \dfrac{- 2 . 303RT}{F}log\dfrac{0 . 01}{0 . 1} = \dfrac{2 . 303RT}{F}$

$\dfrac{{dE}_{cell}}{dT} = \dfrac{2 . 303R}{F}$

$∴ \DeltaS = nF\dfrac{dE}{dT} > 0$

It is an entropy driven process.

(C) It is correct

Racemisation is a thermodynamically favourable method, and it proceeds spontaneously if a suitable pathway is accessible for the interconversion of the enantiomers.

During racemisation of optically active compound, disorderness increases and hence, entropy increases.

(D) For ${\left[Ni{\left({H}_{2}O\right)}_{6}\right]}^{2 +} + 3en \to {\left[Ni{\left(en\right)}_{3}\right]}^{+ 3} + 6{H}_{2}O$
Entropy increases when bidentate ligands replace monodentate ligands due to increase in the number of molecules on the product side.

Hence, (B, C, D) are correct.

26670.text: A closed container contains a homogeneous mixture of two moles of an ideal monatomic gas $\left(\gamma = \dfrac{5}{3}\right)$ and one mole of an ideal diatomic gas $\left(\gamma = \dfrac{7}{5}\right)$. Here, $\gamma$ is the ratio of the specific heats at constant pressure and constant volume of an ideal gas. The gas mixture does a work of $66$ Joule when heated at constant pressure. The change in its internal energy is _____ Joule.
26670.sol:
Change in internal energy for the mixture can be written as,$∆ U = {n}_{1}{\left({C}_{v}\right)}_{1} ∆ T + {n}_{2}{\left({C}_{v}\right)}_{2} ∆ T$

$= \left({n}_{1}{\left({C}_{v}\right)}_{1} + {n}_{2}{\left({C}_{v}\right)}_{2}\right) ∆ T . . . \left(i\right)$

For isobaric process, work done $= P ∆ V$

$= \left({n}_{1} + {n}_{2}\right)R ∆ T . . . \left(ii\right)$

Divide $\left(i\right)$ by $\left(ii\right)$, we get

$\dfrac{∆ U}{W} = \dfrac{\left({n}_{1}{\left({C}_{v}\right)}_{1} + {n}_{2}{\left({C}_{v}\right)}_{2}\right) ∆ T}{\left({n}_{1} + {n}_{2}\right)R ∆ T}$

$⇒ ∆ U = \dfrac{W}{R}\left(\dfrac{\left({n}_{1}{\left({C}_{v}\right)}_{1} + {n}_{2}{\left({C}_{v}\right)}_{2}\right)}{{n}_{1} + {n}_{2}}\right)$

$= \dfrac{66}{R}\dfrac{\left[2 \times \dfrac{3R}{2} + 1 \times \dfrac{5R}{2}\right]}{2 + 1}$

$= 121J$

29128.text:
Highest oxidation state of $Mn$ is exhibited in ${Mn}_{2}{O}_{7}$. The correct statements about ${Mn}_{2}{O}_{7}$ are

(A) $Mn$ is tetrahedrally surrounded by oxygen atoms
(B) $Mn$ is octahedrally surrounded by oxygen atoms
(C) Contains $Mn - O - Mn$ bridge
(D) Contains $Mn - Mn$ bond.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
29128.sol:
Each $Mn$ is tetrahedrally surrounded by oxygen atoms. In addition, there is a bridging two-coordinated oxygen atom between two tetrahedral units. The bridged $Mn - O$ has different bond length than the tetrahedrally surrounded $Mn - O$ bond lengths.

So, the correct statement is only A and C.

29536.text:
Some reactions of ${NO}_{2}$ relevant to photochemical smog formation are

Identify $A, B, X$ and $Y$
29536.sol:
When fossil fuels are burnt, a variety of pollutants are emitted into the earth’s troposphere. Two of the pollutants that are emitted are hydrocarbons (unburnt fuels) and nitric oxide (NO). When these pollutants build up to sufficiently high levels, a chain reaction occurs from their interaction with sunlight in which NO is converted into nitrogen dioxide ${NO}_{2}$. This ${NO}_{2}$ in turn absorbs energy from sunlight and breaks up into nitric oxide and a free oxygen atom.

$N{O}_{2} ( g ) \overset{hν}{\to}NO ( g ) + O ( g )$

Oxygen atoms are very reactive and combine with the ${O}_{2}$ in air to produce ozone.

$O ( g ) + {O}_{2} ( g ) ⇌ {O}_{3} ( g )$

Hence, $X = O, Y = NO, A = {O}_{2}, B = {O}_{3}$

30417.subject: Chemistry
30417.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Benzene is nitrated to give nitrobenzene, which on further treatment with $\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{COCl} / \mathrm{AlCl}_{3}$ will give

Statement II: $-\mathrm{NO}_{2}$ group is a $m$-directing, and deactivating group.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
30417.sol:
Statement I: Benzene reacts with nitrating mixture ($conc. HNO_3 + conc. H_2SO_4$) to form nitrobenzene. However, nitrobenzene is highly deactivated due to the strong electron-withdrawing $-I$ and $-M$ effects of the $-NO_2$ group. Friedel-Crafts reactions (alkylation or acylation) do not occur on strongly deactivated rings like nitrobenzene. Thus, nitrobenzene will not react with $CH_3COCl/AlCl_3$ to give m-nitroacetophenone. Statement I is incorrect.

Statement II: The $-NO_2$ group is a meta-directing group because it withdraws electron density from the ortho and para positions more than from the meta position. It is also a deactivating group as it reduces the overall electron density of the benzene ring, making it less reactive towards electrophilic aromatic substitution. Statement II is correct.

Therefore, Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

31870.text:
$\mathrm{A}+2 \mathrm{~B} \longrightarrow \mathrm{AB}_{2}$
36.0 g of 'A' (Molar mass: $60 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$) and 56.0 g of ' $\mathrm{B}^{\prime}$ (Molar mass: $80 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$) are allowed to react. Which of the following statements are correct ?
A. 'A' is the limiting reagent.
B. $77.0 \mathrm{~g}$ of $\mathrm{AB}_{2}$ is formed.
C. Molar mass of $A B_{2}$ is $140 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$.
D. $15.0 \mathrm{~g}$ of A is left unreacted after the completion of reaction.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
31870.sol:
Reaction: A + 2B → AB₂.
Moles of A = 36.0/60 = 0.6 mol;
Moles of B = 56.0/80 = 0.7 mol.
A requires 1.2 mol of B but only 0.7 available, so B is limiting reagent.
So, (A) False - B is limiting.
(B) AB₂ formed = 0.7/2 = 0.35 mol;
Molar mass AB₂ = 60 + 2(80) = 220 g/mol;
Mass = 0.35 × 220 = 77 g True.
(C) False - Molar mass is 220 g/mol.
(D) A remaining = 0.6 - 0.35 = 0.25 mol = 15 g True.
Correct statements: B and D.

32866.subject: Mathematics
32866.text: The number of distinct real roots of the equation ${x}^{5}\left({x}^{3} - {x}^{2} - x + 1\right) + x\left(3{x}^{3} - 4{x}^{2} - 2x + 4\right) - 1 = 0$ is
32866.sol:
Given,

${x}^{5}\left({x}^{3} - {x}^{2} - x + 1\right) + x\left(3{x}^{3} - 4{x}^{2} - 2x + 4\right) - 1 = 0$

Now on rearranging we get

$⇒ {x}^{8} - {x}^{7} - {x}^{6} + {x}^{5} + 3{x}^{4} - 4{x}^{3} - 2{x}^{2} + 4x - 1 = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{7}\left(x - 1\right) - {x}^{5}\left(x - 1\right) + 3{x}^{3}\left(x - 1\right) - x\left({x}^{2} - 1\right) - 2x\left(x - 1\right) + x - 1 = 0$

$⇒ \left(x - 1\right)\left({x}^{7} - {x}^{5} + 3{x}^{3} - x\left(x + 1\right) - 2x + 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(x - 1\right)\left({x}^{5}\left({x}^{2} - 1\right) + 3x\left({x}^{2} - 1\right) - 1\left({x}^{2} - 1\right)\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left({x}^{2} - 1\right)\left(x - 1\right)\left({x}^{5} + 3x - 1\right) = 0$

From above equation it is clearly visible that the root are $x = \pm 1$ and for ${x}^{5} + 3x - 1$

Let $f\left(x\right) = {x}^{5} + 3x - 1$, ${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = 5{x}^{4} + 3$

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) > 0 ∀ x \in R$, hence it is monotonic in nature so it will have only one root other than $1 \text{ and } - 1$.

Hence $3$ real distinct roots.

33258.text: Let $a, b, c$ be the three distinct positive real numbers such that ${\left(2a\right)}^{{\log}_{e}a} = {\left(bc\right)}^{{\log}_{e}b}$ and ${b}^{{\log}_{e}2} = {a}^{{\log}_{e}c}$ Then $6a + 5bc$ is equal to ______.
33258.sol:
Given equation: ${\left(2a ight)}^{ln\left(a ight)} = {\left(bc ight)}^{ln\left(b ight)}$

$⇒ ln\left(a ight) \cdot \left(ln\left(2a ight) ight) = ln\left(b ight) \cdot ln\left(bc ight)$

$⇒ ln\left(a ight) \cdot \left(ln\left(2 ight) + ln\left(a ight) ight) = ln\left(b ight) \cdot \left(ln\left(b ight) + ln\left(c ight) ight)$

let $ln\left(a ight) = x, ln\left(b ight) = y, ln\left(c ight) = z, x e y e z$

$⇒ x\left(ln\left(2 ight) + x ight) = y\left(y + z ight)$

$⇒ xln\left(2 ight) = {y}^{2} - {x}^{2} + yz$ ........(i)

Similarly, from second equation

$ln\left(2 ight) \cdot ln\left(b ight) = ln\left(c ight) \cdot ln\left(a ight)$

$⇒ ln\left(2 ight) = \dfrac{xz}{y}$ ......(ii)

Substitute $eq\left(ii ight) ext{in}eq\left(i ight)$,

We get,

$⇒ {y}^{3} - y{x}^{2} + {y}^{2}z = {x}^{2}z$

$⇒ {y}^{2}\left(y + z ight) - {x}^{2}\left(y + z ight) = 0$

$⇒ \left({y}^{2} - {x}^{2} ight)\left(y + z ight) = 0$

$⇒ \left(x - y ight)\left(x + y ight)\left(y + z ight) = 0$

$∵ x e y ⇒ \left(x + y ight)\left(y + z ight) = 0$

Now $x = - y, y = - z ext{and}x = z$

But $ln\left(2 ight) = \dfrac{xz}{y}$

$⇒ ln\left(2 ight) = \dfrac{x\left(x ight)}{- x}$

$⇒ ln\left(2 ight) = - ln\left(a ight)$

$= - ln2 ⇒ a = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and

$⇒ y = - z$

$⇒ ln\left(b ight) = - ln\left(c ight)$

$⇒ bc = 1$

Now $6a + 5bc = 6\left(\dfrac{1}{2} ight) + 5\left(1 ight) = 8$

Hence this is the required answer.

33349.text: Let the number $( 22{)}^{2022} + ( 2022{)}^{22}$ leave the remainder $\alpha$ when divided by $3$ and $\beta$ when divided by $7$. Then $( {\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2} )$ is equal to
33349.sol:
Given that $\alpha$ be the remainder when ${\left(22\right)}^{2022} + {\left(2022\right)}^{22}$ is divided by $3$ and $\beta$ be the remainder when the same is divided by $7$.

$⇒ {\left(22\right)}^{2022} + {\left(2022\right)}^{22} = {\left(21 + 1\right)}^{2022} + {\left(2022\right)}^{22}$.

Here ${\left(2022\right)}^{22}$ is divisible by $3$ as $2022$ is divisible by $3$.

So on expanding ${\left(21 + 1\right)}^{2022}$, we get

$⇒ {\left(21 + 1\right)}^{2022} = C0 2022 {\left(21\right)}^{2022} + C1 2022 {\left(21\right)}^{2021} + . . . . . . + C2022 2022 {\left(1\right)}^{2022}$

$= 3\left({3}^{2021} \times {7}^{2022} + C1 2022 \times {3}^{2020} \times {7}^{2021} + . . . . . .\right) + 1$

$= 3{k}_{1} + 1$

In this case the remainder is $1$

Hence, $\alpha = 1$

Now, $⇒ {\left(22\right)}^{2022} + {\left(2022\right)}^{22} = {\left(21 + 1\right)}^{2022} + {\left(2023 - 1\right)}^{22}$

Take ${\left(2023 - 1\right)}^{22}$

$⇒ {\left(2023 - 1\right)}^{22} = C0 22 {\left(2023\right)}^{22} - C1 22 {\left(2023\right)}^{21} + . . . . . . + C22 22 {\left(- 1\right)}^{22}$

$= 7\left(C0 22 {\left(7\right)}^{21}{\left(289\right)}^{22} - C1 22 {\left(7\right)}^{20}{\left(289\right)}^{21} + . . . . . .\right) + 1$

$= 7{k}_{2} + 1$

$⇒ {\left(21 + 1\right)}^{2022} + {\left(2023 - 1\right)}^{22} = 7{k}_{1} + 1 + 7{k}_{2} + 1$

$= 7\mu + 2$

$⇒ \beta = 2$.

Hence, ${\alpha}^{2} + {\beta}^{2} = {1}^{2} + {2}^{2} = 5$.

Therefore, the required answer is $5$.

33931.text: For all complex numbers $z$ of the form $1 + i\alpha, \alpha \in R,$ if ${z}^{2} = x + iy,$ then
33931.sol:
Given $z = 1 + i \alpha, {z}^{2} = x + iy$

$⇒ {\left(1 + i \alpha\right)}^{2} = x + iy$

$⇒ {1}^{2} + {i}^{2}{\alpha}^{2} + 2i\alpha = x + iy$

Using ${i}^{2} = - 1,$

$⇒ 1 - {\alpha}^{2} + 2i\alpha = x + iy$

Equating the real and imaginary parts, we get

$x = 1 - {\alpha}^{2}$ and $y = 2\alpha$

$⇒ {\alpha}^{2} = 1 - x$ and ${y}^{2} = 4{\alpha}^{2}$

$⇒ {y}^{2} = 4\left(1 - x\right)$

$⇒ {y}^{2} = 4 - 4x$

$⇒ {y}^{2} + 4x - 4 = 0 .$

34027.text:
Let $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be defined as $f\left(x\right) = \left[\begin{cases}\left[{e}^{x}\right], & x < 0 \\ a{e}^{x} + \left[x - 1\right], & 0 \le x < 1 \\ b + \left[sin\left(\pix\right)\right], & 1 \le x < 2 \\ \left[{e}^{- x}\right] - c, & x \ge 2\end{cases}\right)
where $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\left[t\right]$ denotes greatest integer less than or equal to $t$. Then, which of the following statements is true?
options: There exists $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $f$ is continuous of $\mathbb{R}$.
If $f$ is discontinuous at exactly one point, then $a + b + c = 1$
If $f$ is discontinuous at exactly one point, then $a + b + c \ne 1$.
$f$ is discontinuous at atleast two points, for any values of $a, b$ and $c$.
34027.sol:
Given $f\left(x\right) = \left[\begin{cases}\left[{e}^{x}\right], & x < 0 \\ a{e}^{x} + \left[x - 1\right], & 0 \le x < 1 \\ b + \left[sin\left(\pix\right)\right], & 1 \le x < 2 \\ \left[{e}^{- x}\right] - c, & x \ge 2\end{cases}\right)

i.e. $f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}0, & x < 0 \\ a{e}^{x} - 1, & 0 \le x < 1 \\ b, & x = 1 \\ b - 1, & 1 < x < 2 \\ - c, & x \ge 2\end{cases}\right)

Here, we know $f\left(x\right)$ is discontinuous at $x = 1$ as $b \ne b - 1$

For $f\left(x\right)$ to be continuous at $x = 0; a = 1$

For $f\left(x\right)$ to be continuous at $x = 2; b + c = 1$

Hence, $a + b + c = 2$

34229.text: Let a differentiable function $f$ satisfy $f\left(x\right) + {∫}_{3}^{x}\dfrac{f\left(t\right)}{t}dt = \sqrt{x + 1}, x \ge 3$. Then $12f\left(8\right)$ is equal to:
34229.sol:
Given:

$f\left(x\right) + {∫}_{3}^{x}\dfrac{f\left(t\right)}{t}dt = \sqrt{x + 1}$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) + \dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{x} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x + 1}}$

Put $y = f\left(x\right)$, then

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{y}{x} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x + 1}}$

So, $I . F . = {e}^{∫ \dfrac{dx}{x}} = {e}^{ln\left|x\right|} = x$

Hence, solution is

$xy = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x + 1}}dx$

$⇒ xy = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \left(\dfrac{x + 1 - 1}{\sqrt{x + 1}}\right)dx$

$⇒ xy = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \left(\sqrt{x + 1} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x + 1}}\right)dx$

$⇒ xy = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\left(x + 1\right)\dfrac{3}{2} - 2\sqrt{x + 1}\right) + C$

$⇒ xy = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(x + 1\right)\dfrac{3}{2} - \sqrt{x + 1} + C$

Put $x = 3$, then $f\left(3\right) = 2$

So,

$6 = \dfrac{8}{3} - 2 + C ⇒ C = \dfrac{16}{3}$

Hence,

$xy = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(x + 1\right)\dfrac{3}{2} - \sqrt{x + 1} + \dfrac{16}{3}$

So, put $x = 8$, then

$8f\left(8\right) = \dfrac{27}{3} - 3 + \dfrac{16}{3}$

$⇒ f\left(8\right) = \dfrac{34}{3 \times 8}$

$⇒ 12f\left(8\right) = 17$

34275.text: The value of the integral $\dfrac{48}{{\pi}^{4}}{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\left(\dfrac{3\pi{x}^{2}}{2} - {x}^{3}\right)\dfrac{sinx}{1 + \cos^{2}x}dx$ is equal to ______.
34275.sol:
Let $I = \dfrac{48}{{\pi}^{4}}{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}{x}^{2} - {x}^{3}\right)\dfrac{sinx}{1 + \cos^{2}x}dx \ldots \left(1\right)$

Using ${∫}_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right)dx = {∫}_{a}^{b}f ( a + b - x ) dx$

We get $I = \dfrac{48}{{\pi}^{4}}{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}{\left(\pi - x\right)}^{2} - {\left(\pi - x\right)}^{3}\right)\dfrac{sin\left(0 + \pi - x\right)}{1 + \cos^{2}\left(0 + \pi - x\right)}dx$

$I = \dfrac{48}{{\pi}^{4}}{∫}_{0}^{\pi}\left(\dfrac{3{\pi}^{3}}{2} - 3{\pi}^{2}x + \dfrac{3\pi{x}^{2}}{2} - {\pi}^{3} + {x}^{3} + 3{\pi}^{2}x - 3\pi{x}^{2}\right)\dfrac{sinx}{1 + \cos^{2}x}dx$ ..............equation $2$

Now adding equation (1) + equation (2)

$⇒ {F}^{'} ( x ) = f ( x )$

$⇒ I = 2\left\{1 - \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{4 !} + \dfrac{1}{6 !} + . . .\right)\right\}$

$⇒ I = 1 - \dfrac{2}{4 !} + \dfrac{2}{6 !} - \dfrac{2}{9 !} . . .$

$⇒ 1 - \dfrac{2}{4 !} < I < 1 - \dfrac{2}{4 !} + \dfrac{2}{6 !}$

$⇒ \dfrac{11}{12} < I < \dfrac{331}{360}$

$x + 2y + 3z = 1$

$D = \left|\begin{cases}3 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 4 & 4\end{cases}\right|\left({R}_{3} \to {R}_{3} - 2{R}_{1} + 3{R}_{2}\right)$

So, for infinite solution $2\mu - 2 = \delta$

$2\mu \ne \delta + 2$

Given $sin\thetatan\theta + tan\theta = sin2\theta; \theta \ne \pm \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\sin^{2}\theta}{cos\theta} + \dfrac{sin\theta}{cos\theta} = 2sin\thetacos\theta$

$⇒ sin\theta = 0$ or $\dfrac{sin\theta}{cos\theta} + \dfrac{1}{cos\theta} = 2cos\theta$

$⇒ \theta = 0, \pi, - \pi$ or $sin\theta + 1 = 2\left(1 - \sin^{2}\theta\right)$

$⇒ \theta = 0, \pi, - \pi$ or $2\sin^{2}\theta + sin\theta - 1 = 0$

$⇒ \theta = 0, \pi, - \pi$ or $sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}, sin\theta = - 1$

$⇒ \theta = 0, \pi, - \pi$ or $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}, \dfrac{5\pi}{6}$ or $\theta = \dfrac{- \pi}{2}$ (rejected)

Hence, $\theta = \left\{0, \pi, - \pi, \dfrac{\pi}{6}, \dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right\}$

$⇒ n\left(S\right) = 5$

Now, $T = Σcos2\theta$

$= cos0 + cos2\pi + cos\left(- 2\pi\right) + cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) + cos\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{3}\right)$

$= 1 + 1 + 1 + \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} = 4$

So, $T + n\left(S\right) = 9$

40132.subject: Physics
40132.text: Three identical coils $C_{1}, C_{2}$ and $C_{3}$ are closely placed such that they share a common axis. $C_{2}$ is exactly midway. $C_{1}$ carries current $I$ in anti-clockwise direction while $C_{3}$ carries current $I$ in clockwise direction. An induced current flows through $C_{2}$ will be in clockwise direction when
options: $C_{1}$ moves away from $C_{2}$ and $C_{3}$ moves towards $C_{2}$
$C_{1}$ and $C_{3}$ move with equal speeds away from $C_{2}$
$C_{1}$ moves towards $C_{2}$ and $C_{3}$ moves away from $C_{2}$
$C_{1}$ and $C_{3}$ move with equal speeds towards $C_{2}$
40132.sol:
Let the common axis be the z-axis.
$C_1$ is at $z = -d$, $C_2$ is at $z = 0$, and $C_3$ is at $z = +d$.
Current in $C_1$ is anti-clockwise (ACW), producing a magnetic field $B_1$ in the $+z$ direction at $C_2$.
Current in $C_3$ is clockwise (CW), producing a magnetic field $B_3$ in the $-z$ direction at $C_2$.
The net magnetic field at $C_2$ is $B_{net} = B_1 - B_3$. Since $C_1$ and $C_3$ are equidistant and carry equal current, initially $B_{net} = 0$.

To induce a clockwise current in $C_2$, Lenz's law states that the induced current must oppose the change in flux. A clockwise induced current produces a magnetic field in the $-z$ direction.
This happens if there is an increasing flux in the $+z$ direction or a decreasing flux in the $-z$ direction.

Case 1: $C_1$ moves towards $C_2$. The distance decreases, so $B_1$ (in $+z$ direction) increases. This causes an increasing flux in the $+z$ direction.

Case 2: $C_3$ moves away from $C_2$. The distance increases, so $B_3$ (in $-z$ direction) decreases. This causes a decreasing flux in the $-z$ direction.

Both actions (moving $C_1$ towards $C_2$ and moving $C_3$ away from $C_2$) result in a net change in flux that induces a clockwise current in $C_2$ to oppose the change.
Therefore, option (3) is correct.

The electric field of an electromagnetic wave travelling through a medium is given by
$\vec{E}(x, t)=25 \sin \left(2.0 \times 10^{15} t-10^{7} x\right) \hat{n}$

40277.sol:
The electric field is $E(x,t) = 25\sin(2.0 \times 10^{15}t - 10^7 x)$ V/m.
This is in the standard form $E = E_0\sin(\omega t - kx)$ where angular frequency $\omega = 2.0 \times 10^{15}$ rad/s and wave number $k = 10^7$ rad/m.
The speed of the wave in the medium is $v = \frac{\omega}{k} = \frac{2.0 \times 10^{15}}{10^7} = 2.0 \times 10^8$ m/s.
The refractive index is defined as $n = \frac{c}{v}$ where $c = 3.0 \times 10^8$ m/s is the speed of light in vacuum.
Therefore, $n = \frac{3.0 \times 10^8}{2.0 \times 10^8} = 1.5$

According to Gauss's law, the electric flux through a closed surface is given by $\Phi = \dfrac{q_{\text{enclosed}}}{\varepsilon_0}$.

For the first sphere of radius $r_1 = 3$ cm centered at the origin, only the charge at $x = 2$ cm is enclosed.

$q_{\text{enclosed}, 1} = 8 \, \mu\text{C}$

$\Phi_1 = \dfrac{8 \, \mu\text{C}}{\varepsilon_0}$

For the second sphere of radius $r_2 = 5$ cm centered at the origin, both charges at $x = 2$ cm and $x = 4$ cm are enclosed.

$q_{\text{enclosed}, 2} = 8 \, \mu\text{C} - 2 \, \mu\text{C} = 6 \, \mu\text{C}$

$\Phi_2 = \dfrac{6 \, \mu\text{C}}{\varepsilon_0}$

The ratio of the electric flux is:

$\dfrac{\Phi_1}{\Phi_2} = \dfrac{8}{6} = \dfrac{4}{3}$

Answer: $4 : 3$

40862.text: Two satellites of masses $m$ and $3m$ revolve around the earth in circular orbits of radii $r \text{ and } 3r$ respectively. The ratio of orbital speeds of the satellites respectively is

The orbital velocity is given

$V = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{GM}{r}\right)}$

where $M$ is the mass of earth and $r$ is the radius of the orbit of satellite.

The velocity of the satellite with mass $m$ is

${V}_{1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{r}}$

and the velocity of the satellite with mass $3m$ is

${V}_{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{3r}}$

Hence, the ratio of the velocities is

$\dfrac{{V}_{1}}{{V}_{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3r}{r}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{1}$

41978.text: A small spherical ball of radius $0 . 1mm$ and density ${10}^{4}kg{m}^{- 3}$ falls freely under gravity through a distance $h$ before entering a tank of water. If, after entering the water the velocity of ball does not change and it continue to fall with same constant velocity inside water, then the value of $h$ will be ____ $m$. (Given $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$, viscosity of water $= 1 . 0 \times {10}^{- 5}N ‐ s{m}^{- 2}$ ).
41978.sol:
Using equation of motion, ${v}^{2} = {u}^{2} + 2as$

${v}^{2} = 0 + 2\left(- g\right)\left(- h\right)$

$⇒ {v}^{2} = 2gh$

Initial velocity of ball is $v = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{20h}$.

If after entering the water this velocity does not change, then this value should be equal to the terminal velocity.

Then, $\sqrt{2gh} = \dfrac{2}{9}\dfrac{{r}^{2}\left(ρ - \sigma\right)g}{η}$, here, $ρ$ is density of ball, $\sigma$ is density of water and $η$ is viscosity.

$⇒ \sqrt{20h} = \dfrac{2}{9}\dfrac{{\left(0 . 1 \times {10}^{- 3}\right)}^{2}\left({10}^{4} - {10}^{3}\right)10}{1 \times {10}^{- 5}} ⇒ \sqrt{20h} = \dfrac{2}{9}\dfrac{{10}^{- 8}\left(10 - 1\right){10}^{3} \times 10}{1 \times {10}^{- 5}}$

$⇒ 20h = 400$

$∴ h = 20m$

42543.subject: Physics
42543.text: A radioactive nucleus decays by two different process. The half life of the first process is $5$ minutes and that of the second process is $30s$. The effective half-life of the nucleus is calculated to be $\dfrac{\alpha}{11}s$. The value of $\alpha$ is ______.
42543.sol:
Decay law for both process can be written as,

$\dfrac{d{N}_{1}}{dt} = - {\lambda}_{1}N . . . Eq ( 1 )$ and

$\dfrac{d{N}_{2}}{dt} = - {\lambda}_{2}N . . . Eq ( 2 )$

Hence, net decay will become

$\dfrac{dN}{dt} = \dfrac{d{N}_{1}}{dt} + \dfrac{d{N}_{2}}{dt} = - ( {\lambda}_{1} + {\lambda}_{2} ) N$

$⇒ {\lambda}_{eq} = {\lambda}_{1} + {\lambda}_{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{ln2}{{t}_{\dfrac{1}{2}}} = \dfrac{ln2}{300} + \dfrac{ln2}{30}$

$⇒ t\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{300}{11}$

Hence, required value of $\alpha = 300$.

44200.subject: Physics
44200.text: A beam of light consisting of wavelengths 650 nm and 550 nm illuminates the Young's double slits with separation of 2 mm such that the interference fringes are formed on a screen, placed at a distance of 1.2 m from the slits. The least distance of a point from the central maximum, where the bright fringes due to both the wavelengths coincide, is $\_\_\_\_$ $\times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~m}$.
44200.sol:
Given wavelengths are $\lambda_1 = 650$ nm and $\lambda_2 = 550$ nm.
Slit separation $d = 2$ mm $= 2 \times 10^{-3}$ m.
Distance to screen $D = 1.2$ m.
For the bright fringes of both wavelengths to coincide at a distance $y$ from the central maximum, we have:
$y = n_1 \frac{\lambda_1 D}{d} = n_2 \frac{\lambda_2 D}{d}$
where $n_1$ and $n_2$ are integers representing the order of the fringes.
This simplifies to $n_1 \lambda_1 = n_2 \lambda_2$.
$\frac{n_1}{n_2} = \frac{\lambda_2}{\lambda_1} = \frac{550}{650} = \frac{11}{13}$
The least values for coincidence are $n_1 = 11$ and $n_2 = 13$.
The least distance $y$ is given by:
$y = n_1 \frac{\lambda_1 D}{d} = 11 \times \frac{650 \times 10^{-9} \times 1.2}{2 \times 10^{-3}}$
$y = 11 \times 650 \times 0.6 \times 10^{-6}$ m
$y = 11 \times 390 \times 10^{-6}$ m
$y = 4290 \times 10^{-6}$ m
$y = 429 \times 10^{-5}$ m.

46176.subject: Physics
46176.text: A photosensitive metallic surface has work function, $h v_0$. If photons of energy $2 h v_0$ fall on this surface, the electrons come out with a maximum velocity of $4 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. When the photon energy is increased to $5 h v_0$, then maximum velocity of photoelectrons will be
46176.sol:
The solution to our problem consists in Einstein's photoelectric equation.
Einstein's photoelectric equation can be written as $\frac{1}{2} m v^2=h v-\phi$
$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} m \times\left(4 \times 10^6\right)^2=2 h v_0-h v_0...(i)$
and $\frac{1}{2} m \times v^2=5 h v_0-h v_0...(ii)$
Dividing Eq. (ii) by Eq. (i), we get
$\frac{v^2}{\left(4 \times 10^6\right)^2}=\frac{4 h v_0}{h v_0}$
$\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & v^2=4 \times 16 \times 10^{12} \\ \Rightarrow & v^2=64 \times 10^{12} \\ \therefore & v=8 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\end{array}$
NOTE: The efficiency of photoelectric effect is less than $1 \%$.ie, number of photons less than $1 \%$ are capable of ejecting photoelectrons.

46577.subject: Physics
46577.text: Find ratio of radius of gyration of a disk and ring of same radii at their tangential axis in plane.
46577.sol:
For disk, moment of inertia about the diameter, $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{d}}=\frac{\mathrm{mr}^2}{4}$ and moment of inertia about the tangential axis
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{I}_{\text{disc }}=\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{d}}+\mathrm{mr}^2 \\ & \mathrm{I}_{\text{disc }}=\frac{\mathrm{mr}^2}{4}+\mathrm{mr}^2 \\ & \mathrm{I}_{\text{disc }}=\frac{5 \mathrm{mr}^2}{4}\end{aligned}$
Let the radius of gyration of disc is $\mathrm{k}_{\text{disc }}$.
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{I}_{\text{disc }} & =\mathrm{mk}_{\text{disc }}^2 \\ \frac{5 \mathrm{mr}^2}{4} & =\mathrm{mk}_{\text{disc }}^2 \\ \mathrm{k}_{\text{disc }}^2 & =\sqrt{\frac{5}{4} \mathrm{r}}\end{aligned}$
For ring, moment of inertia about the diameter
$\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{a}}^{\prime}=\mathrm{mr}^2 / 2$
and moment of inertia about the tangential axis
$\mathrm{I}_{\text{ring }}=\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{a}}^{\prime}+\mathrm{mr}^2=\frac{\mathrm{mr}^2}{2}+\mathrm{mr}^2=\frac{3}{2} \mathrm{mr}^2$
Let the radius of gyration of ring $\mathrm{k}_{\text{ring }}$.
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{I}_{\text{ring }} & =\mathrm{mk}^2 \text{ ring } \\ \frac{3}{2} \mathrm{mr}^2 & =\mathrm{mk}^2 \text{ ring } \\ \mathrm{k}_{\text{ring }} & =\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}} \mathrm{r} \\ \frac{\mathrm{k}_{\text{disc }}}{\mathrm{k}_{\text{ring }}} & =\frac{\sqrt{\frac{5}{4} \mathrm{r}}}{\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}} \mathrm{r}}=\sqrt{\frac{5}{6}}\end{aligned}$

47168.text: A man and a woman, who do not show any apparent signs of a certain inherited disease, have seven children (2 daughters and 5 sons). Three of the sons suffer from the given disease but none of the daughters are affected. Which of the following mode of inheritance do you suggest for this disease?
47168.sol: A genetic characteristic that is determined by genes located on the sex chromosomes ( X or Y ) are called sex linked characteristic and the condition where expression of sex linked genes is limited to one sex is called sex limited characteristics. In given problem, disease is the result of sex-linked recessive genes. As neither man nor woman shows signs of disease it means woman would be carrier for disease causing gene. In their children none of the daughter is suffering from disease, while the sons are suffering, it means daughters are also carrier, i.e, X-linked recessive. Suppose, genotype of man $=\mathrm{XY}$ Genotype of woman $=\mathrm{X}^{\mathrm{d}} \mathrm{X}$ (d-disease causing gene) For each delivery the probability for each combination is $25 \%$. So, among seven children 2 normal daughter, 3 diseased sons and 2 normal sons are possible.

48553.text: If $\sin ^{-1} a$ is the acute angle between the curves $x^{2}+y^{2}=4 x$ and $x^{2}+y^{2}=8$ at $(2,2)$, then $a$ is equal to
48553.sol:
Given curves are,
$x^{2}+y^{2}=4 x...(i)$
On differentiating w.r.t. $x$, we get
$2 x+2 y \frac{d y}{d x}=4\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{2-x}{y}$
At $(2,2), \quad\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)_{(2,2)}=\frac{2-0}{2}=0=m_{1}$
and $\quad x^{2}+y^{2}=8$
On differentiating w.r.t. $x$, we get
$\begin{aligned}
2 x+2 y \frac{d y}{d x} &=0 \\
\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x} &=\frac{-x}{y}
\end{aligned}$
At $(2,2)\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)_{(2,2)}=\frac{-2}{2}=-1=m_{2}$
Let $\theta$ be an acute angle between the given curves, then, we get
$\begin{array}{cc} & \tan \theta=\left|\frac{m_{1}-m_{2}}{1+m_{1} \cdot m_{2}}\right|=\left|\frac{0+1}{1+0}\right|=1 \\
\Rightarrow & \tan \theta=\tan 45^{{}^{\circ}} \\
\Rightarrow & \theta=45^{{}^{\circ}}
\end{array}
$\Rightarrow \quad \sin ^{-1}(a)=45^{{}^{\circ}} \quad$ (given \left.\theta=\sin ^{-1}$ a\right)\Rightarrow \quad a=\sin 45^{{}^{\circ}}\therefore \quad a=$\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{\overset{¯}{z}z}{z}\right)2 + \left(\dfrac{\overset{¯}{w}w}{w}\right)2 = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{z2} + \dfrac{1}{w2} = 1 ⇒ z^{2} + w^{2} = z^{2}w^{2}$

 $⇒ z^{2}w^{2} = 1 . . . ( ii )$

$∵$ The number of solution of equations $x^{2} + y^{2} = 1 and x^{2}y^{2} = 1$ is eight 

$∴$ Number of ordered pair $\left(z, w\right)$ is also eight.

Amylose consists of D-glucose units connected by $\alpha$-$1,4$ glycosidic bonds, where the anomeric carbon (C-1) of one glucose is linked to C-4 of the adjacent unit in the $\alpha$ configuration.

58062.sol:
For an acidic buffer,
$\begin{array}{ll}
\therefore & \mathrm{pH}=\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}+\log \frac{[\text{ Salt }]}{[\text{ Acid }]} \\
& (\because[\text{ Salt }]=[\text{ Acid }]) \\
\therefore \quad & \mathrm{pH}=\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}=-\log \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}=-\log \left(1.8 \times 10^{-5}\right) \\
\therefore \quad & \mathrm{pH}=-[\log 1.8-5 \log 10]=4.7447
\end{array}$

58310.text: What is the highest oxidation state possessed by phosphorus in it's oxyacids?
58310.sol: $+5+5$ is the highest oxidation state possessed by phosphorus in it's oxyacids. In oxoacids phosphorus is tetrahedrally surrounded by other atoms. All these acid contains at least one $\mathrm{P}=$ O bond and one $\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{OH}$ bond. 58406.subject: Chemistry
58406.text: Name the catalyst used in the manufacture of HDPE polymer.
58406.sol:
High-density polyethylene (HDPE) is manufactured by the coordination polymerization of ethene using a Ziegler-Natta catalyst.

The Ziegler-Natta catalyst is a mixture of triethyl aluminum, $(C_2H_5)_3Al$, and titanium tetrachloride, $TiCl_4$.

Answer: Triethyl aluminum with titanium tetrachloride

63167.subject: Mathematics
63167.sol:
Given $A = \begin{bmatrix} 5a & -b \\ 3 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$.

Using the property $A(\text{adj } A) = |A|I$, the given equation becomes $AA^T = |A|I$.

$|A| = (5a)(2) - (-b)(3) = 10a + 3b$

$AA^T = \begin{bmatrix} 5a & -b \\ 3 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 5a & 3 \\ -b & 2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 25a^2 + b^2 & 15a - 2b \\ 15a - 2b & 13 \end{bmatrix}$

Equating $AA^T$ to $|A|I$:

$\begin{bmatrix} 25a^2 + b^2 & 15a - 2b \\ 15a - 2b & 13 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 10a + 3b & 0 \\ 0 & 10a + 3b \end{bmatrix}$

From the off-diagonal elements:

$15a - 2b = 0 \Rightarrow b = \dfrac{15a}{2}$

From the bottom-right elements:

$10a + 3b = 13$

Substituting $b = \dfrac{15a}{2}$ into the equation:

$10a + 3\left(\dfrac{15a}{2}\right) = 13$

$\dfrac{20a + 45a}{2} = 13$

$\dfrac{65a}{2} = 13 \Rightarrow a = \dfrac{26}{65} = \dfrac{2}{5}$

Substituting $a = \dfrac{2}{5}$ to find $b$:

$b = \dfrac{15}{2} \left(\dfrac{2}{5}\right) = 3$

$5a + b = 5\left(\dfrac{2}{5}\right) + 3 = 2 + 3 = 5$

Answer: $5$

63963.subject: Mathematics
63963.text: In triangle ABC, with usual notations, if the angles are in Arithmetic Progression and $3c^2 = 2b^2$, then the measure of angle A is
63963.sol:
Given that the angles $A, B, C$ of the triangle are in Arithmetic Progression.

$2B = A + C$

Since $A + B + C = \pi$, we have:

$3B = \pi \Rightarrow B = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

We are given the relation $3c^2 = 2b^2$.

Using the Sine Rule, $b = 2R \sin B$ and $c = 2R \sin C$, we can substitute these into the given relation:

$3(2R \sin C)^2 = 2(2R \sin B)^2$

$3 \sin^2 C = 2 \sin^2 B$

Substituting $B = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ and $\sin B = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$:

$3 \sin^2 C = 2 \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2$

$3 \sin^2 C = 2 \times \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

$\sin^2 C = \dfrac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \sin C = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ (since $\sin C > 0$ for angles in a triangle)

This gives $C = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ or $C = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$.

If $C = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$, then $B + C = \dfrac{\pi}{3} + \dfrac{3\pi}{4} = \dfrac{13\pi}{12} > \pi$, which is not possible for a triangle.

Thus, $C = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

The measure of angle $A$ is:

$A = \pi - (B + C) = \pi - \left(\dfrac{\pi}{3} + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \pi - \dfrac{7\pi}{12} = \dfrac{5\pi}{12}$

64211.text: If the line $3 x+4 y-24=0$ intersects $X$ and $Y$ axes in points $A$ and $B$ respectively then incenter of the triangle $O A B$ where $O$ is origin is
64211.sol:
Incenter of triangle $OAB$ with vertices at intercepts of line $3x+4y-24=0$

The line $3x+4y-24=0$ intersects the axes at $A(8,0)$ (x-intercept) and $B(0,6)$ (y-intercept), with $O=(0,0)$.

Triangle $OAB$ is right-angled at $O$ with side lengths: $OA=8$, $OB=6$, and hypotenuse $AB=10$.

Using the incenter coordinate formula with $a=10$ opposite $O$, $b=6$ opposite $A$, and $c=8$ opposite $B$:

$x = \frac{10\cdot0 + 6\cdot8 + 8\cdot0}{10+6+8} = \frac{48}{24} = 2$

$y = \frac{10\cdot0 + 6\cdot0 + 8\cdot6}{10+6+8} = \frac{48}{24} = 2$

Alternatively, for a right triangle with legs $8$ and $6$, the inradius is $r = \frac{8+6-10}{2} = 2$, confirming the incenter lies at $(r,r)=(2,2)$.

Final answer: $\boxed{(2,2)}$

64826.text: If $\cos(p\theta) + \cos(q\theta) = 0$ and $p \neq q$, then the general value of $\theta$ (where n is any integer) is...
64826.sol:
Given $\cos(p\theta) + \cos(q\theta) = 0$

Using the formula $\cos C + \cos D = 2\cos\left(\dfrac{C+D}{2}\right)\cos\left(\dfrac{C-D}{2}\right)$:

$2\cos\left(\dfrac{p+q}{2}\theta\right)\cos\left(\dfrac{p-q}{2}\theta\right) = 0$

This implies either $\cos\left(\dfrac{p+q}{2}\theta\right) = 0$ or $\cos\left(\dfrac{p-q}{2}\theta\right) = 0$

If $\cos\left(\dfrac{p+q}{2}\theta\right) = 0$, then $\dfrac{p+q}{2}\theta = (2n+1)\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, where $n$ is an integer.

$\theta = \dfrac{(2n+1)\pi}{p+q}$

If $\cos\left(\dfrac{p-q}{2}\theta\right) = 0$, then $\dfrac{p-q}{2}\theta = (2n+1)\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, where $n$ is an integer.

$\theta = \dfrac{(2n+1)\pi}{p-q}$

Combining both cases, the general value of $\theta$ is $\dfrac{(2n+1)\pi}{p \pm q}$

Answer: $\dfrac{(2n+1)\pi}{p \pm q}$

65189.text: The lines $\overline{\mathrm{r}}=\bar{a}+\lambda(\overline{\mathrm{b}} \times \overline{\mathrm{c}})$ and $\overline{\mathrm{r}}=\overline{\mathrm{c}}+\lambda(\bar{a} \times \overline{\mathrm{b}})$ will intersect if
65189.sol:
Given lines:
$L_1: \vec{r} = \vec{a} + \lambda (\vec{b} \times \vec{c})$
$L_2: \vec{r} = \vec{c} + \mu (\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$

For intersection, there exist $\lambda$, $\mu$ such that $\vec{a} + \lambda (\vec{b} \times \vec{c}) = \vec{c} + \mu (\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$.

Dot both sides with $\vec{b}$:

$\vec{b} \cdot \vec{a} + \lambda [\vec{b} \cdot (\vec{b} \times \vec{c})] = \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + \mu [\vec{b} \cdot (\vec{a} \times \vec{b})]$

Since scalar triple products with repeated vectors vanish,

$\vec{b} \cdot \vec{a} = \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}$

This is necessary for intersection.

The general intersection condition is $(\vec{a}_2 - \vec{a}_1) \cdot (\vec{d}_1 \times \vec{d}_2) = 0$. Here, $\vec{a}_1 = \vec{a}$, $\vec{d}_1 = \vec{b} \times \vec{c}$, $\vec{a}_2 = \vec{c}$, $\vec{d}_2 = \vec{a} \times \vec{b}$.

Compute $(\vec{b} \times \vec{c}) \times (\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) = -[\vec{a} \vec{b} \vec{c}] \vec{b}$ using vector triple product identity.

The condition becomes:

$(\vec{c} - \vec{a}) \cdot \left(-[\vec{a} \vec{b} \vec{c}] \vec{b}\right) = 0$

$-[\vec{a} \vec{b} \vec{c}] (\vec{c} \cdot \vec{b} - \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}) = 0$

This holds if $[\vec{a} \vec{b} \vec{c}] = 0$ or $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = \vec{c} \cdot \vec{b}$.

Since $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}$ is both necessary and sufficient, it is the required condition.

65867.text: In the hydrogen atom, radii of the first four Bohr orbits are related as
65867.sol:
The radius of the $n$-th Bohr orbit in a hydrogen-like atom is given by $r_n = \dfrac{n^2 h^2 \epsilon_0}{\pi m e^2 Z}$.

For a hydrogen atom, $Z = 1$, which implies $r_n \propto n^2$.

For the first four orbits, $n = 1, 2, 3, 4$.

The ratio of their radii is $r_1 : r_2 : r_3 : r_4 = 1^2 : 2^2 : 3^2 : 4^2 = 1 : 4 : 9 : 16$.

Answer: $1 : 4 : 9 : 16$

66065.text: A $4 \mu \mathrm{ F}$ capacitor is charged to 10 V. The battery is then disconnected and a pure 10 mH coil is connected across the capacitor so that LC oscillations are set up. The maximum current in the coil is
66065.sol:
In an LC circuit, energy conservation requires that the maximum current occurs when all initial capacitor energy transfers to the inductor. The initial energy stored in the capacitor is $U_C = \frac{1}{2}CV^2 = \frac{1}{2}(4 \times 10^{-6}\ \mathrm{F})(10\ \mathrm{V})^2 = 2 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{J}$.

When the current reaches its maximum $I_{\text\max}$, the inductor energy equals the initial capacitor energy: $\frac{1}{2}LI_{\text\max^2 = \frac{1}{2}CV^2$. Solving for $I_{\text\max}$ yields $I_{\text\max} = V\sqrt{\frac{C}{L}}$.

Substituting $L = 10\ \mathrm{mH} = 10^{-2}\ \mathrm{H}$ gives $I_{\text\max} = 10\ \mathrm{V}\sqrt{\frac{4 \times 10^{-6}\ \mathrm{F}}{10^{-2}\ \mathrm{H}}} = 10\sqrt{4 \times 10^{-4}} = 10 \times 0.02 = 0.2\ \mathrm{A}$.

Final answer: $\boxed{0.2\ \mathrm{A}}$

67207.subject: Physics
67207.text: Time period of a simple pendulum is $T_1$ when on the earth's surface and $T_2$ when taken to a height '2R' above the earth's surface, where 'R' is the radius of the earth. The ratio $T_1 : T_2$ is
67207.sol:
The time period of a simple pendulum is given by $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g}}$.

The acceleration due to gravity at a distance $r$ from the center of the earth is $g = \dfrac{GM}{r^2}$.

Substituting this into the time period formula gives $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{L r^2}{GM}}$, which implies $T \propto r$.

On the surface of the earth, the distance from the center is $r_1 = R$, so $T_1 \propto R$.

At a height $h = 2R$ above the surface, the distance from the center is $r_2 = R + 2R = 3R$, so $T_2 \propto 3R$.

The ratio of the time periods is $\dfrac{T_1}{T_2} = \dfrac{R}{3R} = \dfrac{1}{3}$.

Thus, $T_1 : T_2 = 1 : 3$.

Answer: $1 : 3$

67995.text: The maximum error in the measurement of the density and mass of the uniform cube are 8% and 2% respectively. Hence, the maximum error in the measurement of length will be
67995.sol:
The density of a uniform cube is given by the formula:

$\rho = \dfrac{M}{V} = \dfrac{M}{L^3}$

The maximum percentage error in the measurement of density is given by the sum of the percentage errors of the individual measured quantities:

$\dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} \times 100 = \dfrac{\Delta M}{M} \times 100 + 3 $\$left(\dfrac{\Delta L}{L} \times100\right)$

Given that the maximum percentage error in density is $8\%$ and the maximum percentage error in mass is $2\%$, substituting these values yields:

$8\% = 2\% + 3 \left(\dfrac{\Delta L}{L} \times100\right)$

$3 \left(\dfrac{\Delta L}{L} \times100\right) = 8\% - 2\% = 6\%$

$\dfrac{\Delta L}{L} \times100 = 2\%$

Therefore, the maximum error in the measurement of length is $2\%$.

Answer: $2\%$$

68161.text: Water rises in a capillary tube of radius $r$ upto a height $h$. The mass of water in a capillary is $m$. The mass of water that will rise in capillary of radius $\frac{\mathrm{r}}{5}$ will be
68161.sol:
The height to which water rises in a capillary tube of radius $r$ is given by $h = \frac{2T \cos\theta}{\rho g r}$, where $T$ is surface tension, $\theta$ is the contact angle, $\rho$ is density, and $g$ is gravitational acceleration. Therefore, $h \propto \frac{1}{r}$, so $hr$ is constant.

The mass of water in the capillary is $m = \rho V = \rho \pi r^2 h$. Substituting $h = \frac{\text{constant}}{r}$, we obtain $m = \rho \pi r^2 \left(\frac{\text{constant}}{r}\right) = (\rho \pi \cdot\text{constant}) r$. Thus, $m \propto r$.

For a new radius $r_2 = \frac{r}{5}$, the mass $m_2$ satisfies $\frac{m_2}{m} = \frac{r_2}{r} = \frac{1}{5}$. Consequently, $m_2 = \frac{m}{5}$.

The mass of water that rises in the capillary of radius $\frac{r}{5}$ is $\frac{m}{5}$. The correct option is A.

68708.subject: Physics
68708.text: A particle is executing linear S.H.M. starting from mean position. The ratio of the kinetic energy to the potential energy of the particle at a point of half the amplitude is
68708.sol:
For a particle performing simple harmonic motion with amplitude $A$ and angular frequency $\omega$, whose displacement from mean position is $x$, the force constant is given by $k = m\omega^2$.

The potential energy at displacement $x$ is $PE = \frac{1}{2} k x^2$, while the kinetic energy is $KE = \frac{1}{2} m\omega^2 (A^2 - x^2) = \frac{1}{2} k (A^2 - x^2)$.

At the point where the displacement is half the amplitude, $x = A/2$, the potential energy becomes $PE = \frac{1}{2} k (A/2)^2 = \frac{1}{8} k A^2$
and the kinetic energy becomes $KE = \frac{1}{2} k (A^2 - (A/2)^2) = \frac{1}{2} k (3A^2/4) = \frac{3}{8} k A^2$.

The ratio of kinetic to potential energy is therefore $\frac{KE}{PE} = \frac{3/8}{1/8} = 3$.

Ratio: 3:1
The correct option is B.

69183.subject: Physics
69183.text: A same torque is applied to a disc and a ring of equal mass and radii then
options: the ring will rotate with greater angular frequency.
both will rotate with same angular frequency.
the disc will rotate with greater angular frequency.
both will rotate with same angular velocity.
69183.sol:
Rotational dynamics analysis shows that for a constant applied torque $\tau$, the angular acceleration $\alpha$ relates to moment of inertia $I$ through $\tau = I\alpha$.

For identical mass and radius, a disc has $I_{\text{disc}} = \frac{1}{2}MR^2$ while a ring has $I_{\text{ring}} = MR^2$, establishing $I_{\text{ring}} = 2I_{\text{disc}}$.

With $\tau$ constant, $I\alpha$ remains equal for both objects. Since $I_{\text{ring}} > I_{\text{disc}}$, it follows that $\alpha_{\text{disc}} > \alpha_{\text{ring}}$. From the inertia ratio, $\alpha_{\text{disc}} = 2\alpha_{\text{ring}}$.

Starting from rest, angular frequency evolves as $\omega = \alpha t$. The disc's greater angular acceleration produces higher angular frequency over any duration $t$.

69192.subject: Physics
69192.text: Two discs of moment of inertia ' $\mathrm{I}_1$ ' and ' $\mathrm{I}_2$ ' and angular speeds ' $\omega_1{ }^{\prime}$ and ' $\omega_2$ ' are rotating along the collinear axes passing through their centre of mass and perpendicular to their plane. If the two discs are made to rotate together along the same axis. The rotational kinetic energy of the system will be
69192.sol:
Conservation of angular momentum applies since no external torques act on the system.

The initial angular momentum is $L_i = I_1 \omega_1 + I_2 \omega_2$.

When rotating together, the combined moment of inertia becomes $I_f = I_1 + I_2$ with common angular speed $\omega_f$. The final angular momentum is $L_f = (I_1 + I_2)\omega_f$.

Equating $L_i = L_f$ gives:

$I_1 \omega_1 + I_2 \omega_2 = (I_1 + I_2)\omega_f$

Solving for $\omega_f$:

$\omega_f = \frac{I_1 \omega_1 + I_2 \omega_2}{I_1 + I_2}$

The final kinetic energy is:

$K_f = \frac{1}{2}(I_1 + I_2)\omega_f^2 = \frac{1}{2}(I_1 + I_2) \left( \frac{I_1 \omega_1 + I_2 \omega_2}{I_1 + I_2} \right)^2$

Simplifying:

$K_f = \frac{(I_1 \omega_1 + I_2 \omega_2)^2}{2(I_1 + I_2)}$

This matches option D.

69747.subject: Physics
69747.text: A rectangular black body of temperature $127^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ has surface area $4 \mathrm{ cm} \times 2 \mathrm{ cm}$ and rate of radiation is E. If its temperature is increased by $400^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ and surface area is reduced to half of the initial value then the rate of radiation is
69747.sol:
Radiation rate from a black body follows Stefan-Boltzmann Law: $P = \sigma A T^4$.

Initial temperature is $T_1 = 127^{}^{\circ}\mathrm{C} = 400\mathrm{K}$ with surface area $A_1 = 8\mathrm{cm}^2$ and radiation rate $E = \sigma A_1 T_1^4$.

Final conditions: $T_2 = 127^{}^{\circ}\mathrm{C} + 400^{}^{\circ}\mathrm{C} = 527^{}^{\circ}\mathrm{C} = 800\mathrm{K}$, and $A_2 = \frac{1}{2}A_1 = 4\mathrm{cm}^2$, giving $E' = \sigma A_2 T_2^4$.

The ratio is $\frac{E'}{E} = \frac{A_2}{A_1} \left(\frac{T_2}{T_1}\right)^4 = \frac{1}{2} \left(\frac{800}{400}\right)^4 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 2^4 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 16 = 8$.

New rate is $\boxed{8E}$.

70136.text: In an optical instrument- microscope, the wavelength of light used are $\lambda_1 = 6800$ Å and $\lambda_2 = 5100$ Å. The ratio of the resolving power of microscope corresponding to '$\lambda_1$' to that for '$\lambda_2$' is
70136.sol:
The resolving power of a microscope is given by the formula:

$RP = \dfrac{2 \mu \sin \theta}{\lambda}$

This shows that the resolving power is inversely proportional to the wavelength of the light used:

$RP \propto \dfrac{1}{\lambda}$

The ratio of the resolving power for $\lambda_1$ to that for $\lambda_2$ is:

$\dfrac{RP_1}{RP_2} = \dfrac{\lambda_2}{\lambda_1}$

Substituting the given values $\lambda_1 = 6800$ and $\lambda_2 = 5100$:

$\dfrac{RP_1}{RP_2} = \dfrac{5100}{6800} = \dfrac{51}{68} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

The ratio is $3:4$.

70514.text: The frequency of a stretched uniform wire of length $L$ under tension is in resonance with the fundamental frequency of a closed pipe of same length. If the tension in the wire is increased by 8 N , it is in resonance with the first overtone of the same closed pipe. The initial tension in the wire is
70514.sol:
The fundamental frequency of a stretched wire is given by $f_{\text{wire}} = \frac{1}{2L} \sqrt{T / \mu}$, and that of a closed pipe is $f_{\text{pipe,0}} = v / (4L)$.

Initially, resonance occurs between the wire's fundamental and the pipe's fundamental: $\frac{1}{2L} \sqrt{T_1 / \mu} = v / (4L)$. Simplifying yields $\sqrt{T_1 / \mu} = v / 2$, so $T_1 = \mu v^2 / 4$.

After increasing tension by 8 N, $T_2 = T_1 + 8$, resonance occurs with the pipe's first overtone at $3v / (4L)$: $\frac{1}{2L} \sqrt{T_2 / \mu} = 3v / (4L)$. This simplifies to $\sqrt{T_2 / \mu} = 3v / 2$, giving $T_2 = 9 \mu v^2 / 4$.

Dividing the expressions for $T_2$ and $T_1$ results in $T_2 / T_1 = 9$. Substituting $T_2 = T_1 + 8$ leads to $(T_1 + 8) / T_1 = 9$, hence $T_1 + 8 = 9T_1$, $8 = 8T_1$, and $T_1 = 1$ N.

The initial tension is 1 N.

The given equation is $y=A \sin 2(\omega t-k x)\therefore \quad$ Velocity of the particle, $\mathrm{v}=\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dt}}=2 \mathrm{ A} \omega \cos 2(\omega \mathrm{t}-\mathrm{kx})\therefore \quad$ Maximum velocity $=2 \mathrm{ A} \omega$
Velocity of the wave $=\frac{\omega}{\mathrm{k}}$
Given 2A $\omega=\frac{\omega}{\mathrm{k}}\therefore \quad A=\frac{1}{2 k}=\frac{\lambda}{(2 \pi)^2}=\frac{\lambda}{4 \pi}$

71813.subject: Chemistry
71813.text: Identify the alkane having two secondary carbon atoms.:
71813.sol:
A secondary carbon atom is one that is directly bonded to exactly two other carbon atoms.

Let us analyze the given options:

1. Cyclohexane: All 6 carbon atoms in the ring are bonded to two other carbon atoms. Thus, it has 6 secondary carbon atoms.

2. 1,2,3,4-Tetramethylcyclohexane: The carbon atoms at positions 1, 2, 3, and 4 of the ring are tertiary (each bonded to two ring carbons and one methyl carbon). The carbon atoms at positions 5 and 6 are secondary (each bonded to two ring carbons). The four methyl carbons are primary. Thus, it has exactly two secondary carbon atoms.

3. 1-Ethyl-2,3,4-trimethylcyclohexane: The ring carbons at positions 5 and 6 are secondary. Additionally, the $-CH_2-$ group of the ethyl substituent is also a secondary carbon (bonded to the ring and a methyl group). Thus, it has three secondary carbon atoms.

4. 2,4-Dimethylheptane: The structure is $CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$. The carbons at positions 3, 5, and 6 of the parent chain are secondary. Thus, it has three secondary carbon atoms.

Therefore, 1,2,3,4-Tetramethylcyclohexane is the only compound with exactly two secondary carbon atoms.

Answer: 1,2,3,4-Tetramethylcyclohexane

71915.sol:
Nylon-6,6 is a condensation polymer formed by the reaction of hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid. During this polymerization, amide linkages ($-CO-NH-$) are formed between the monomers. Therefore, Nylon-6,6 is classified as a polyamide polymer.

Teflon (polytetrafluoroethylene) and polythene are addition polymers.

Bakelite is a phenol-formaldehyde resin, which is a cross-linked condensation polymer but does not contain amide linkages.

Answer: Nylon-6,6

72334.subject: Physics
72334.text: A particle executes a linear S.H.M of amplitude 3 cm. When it is at 1 cm from the mean position, the magnitude of its velocity is half that of its acceleration at the point. The maximum velocity is
72334.sol:
Amplitude $A = 3$ cm.

Magnitude of velocity at distance $x$ from the mean position is $v = \omega \sqrt{A^2 - x^2}$.

Magnitude of acceleration at distance $x$ is $a = \omega^2 x$.

Given that at $x = 1$ cm, $v = \dfrac{1}{2} a$.

$\omega \sqrt{3^2 - 1^2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \omega^2 (1)$

$\omega \sqrt{8} = \dfrac{1}{2} \omega^2$

$\omega = 2\sqrt{8} = 4\sqrt{2}$ rad/s.

Maximum velocity is $v_{\max} = A\omega$.

$v_{\max} = 3 \times 4\sqrt{2} = 12\sqrt{2}$ cm/s.

Answer: $12\sqrt{2}$ cm/s

73870.subject: General Ability
73870.text: Which one of the following statements for second law of motion is NOT correct?
options: The net force on a body is proportional to that body's acceleration
The net force on a body is in the same direction as the acceleration
The time rate of change of momentum is equal to force
The net force on a body is proportional to that body's momentum
73870.sol:
According to Newton's second law of motion, the rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied force and takes place in the direction in which the force acts.

Mathematically, $\vec{F} = \dfrac{d\vec{p}}{dt}$.

For a body of constant mass, $\vec{F} = m\vec{a}$. This implies that the net force is proportional to the acceleration and acts in the same direction as the acceleration.

The net force is proportional to the time rate of change of momentum, not to the momentum itself. Therefore, the statement that the net force on a body is proportional to that body's momentum is incorrect.

Answer: The net force on a body is proportional to that body's momentum

76370.subject: Mathematics
76370.text:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The function $f(x) = \dfrac{x^3 + 128}{x}$ has a minimum value 48 at $x = 4$.
Statement-II: As $x$ increases through 4, $f'(x)$ changes sign from positive to negative.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is not correct
Statement-I is not correct but Statement-II is correct
76370.sol:
Given $f(x) = \dfrac{x^3 + 128}{x} = x^2 + \dfrac{128}{x}$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:
$f'(x) = 2x - \dfrac{128}{x^2} = \dfrac{2(x^3 - 64)}{x^2}$

For critical points, $f'(x) = 0$
$\Rightarrow x^3 - 64 = 0 \Rightarrow x = 4$

At $x = 4$, $f(4) = \dfrac{4^3 + 128}{4} = \dfrac{192}{4} = 48$

Now, checking the sign of $f'(x)$ around $x = 4$:
For $x < 4$, $x^3 < 64 \Rightarrow f'(x) < 0$ (negative)
For $x > 4$, $x^3 > 64 \Rightarrow f'(x) > 0$ (positive)

Since $f'(x)$ changes sign from negative to positive as $x$ increases through $4$, $x = 4$ is a point of local minimum. The minimum value is $48$.

Thus, Statement-I is correct.

Statement-II claims that $f'(x)$ changes sign from positive to negative, which is incorrect.

Therefore, Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is not correct.

Answer: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is not correct

77028.subject: Mathematics
77028.text: If $k$ is an arbitrary constant, then what is the general solution of the equation $(x + y)^2 \dfrac{dy}{dx} = k^2$?
77028.sol:
Let $x + y = v$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get $1 + \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dv}{dx} \Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dv}{dx} - 1$

Substituting in the given differential equation:

$v^2 \left( \dfrac{dv}{dx} - 1 \right) = k^2$

$v^2 \dfrac{dv}{dx} = v^2 + k^2$

$\dfrac{v^2}{v^2 + k^2} dv = dx$

$\left( 1 - \dfrac{k^2}{v^2 + k^2} \right) dv = dx$

Integrating both sides:

$\int \left( 1 - \dfrac{k^2}{v^2 + k^2} \right) dv = \int dx$

$v - k \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{v}{k}\right) = x + c$

Substituting $v = x + y$:

$x + y - k \tan^{-1} \left(\dfrac{x + y}{k}\right) =$x + c$

$y - c = k \tan^{-1}$\left(\dfrac{x + y}{k}\right)

\dfrac{y - c}{k} = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x + y}{k}\right)$

$x + y = k \tan \left(\dfrac{y - c}{k}\right)

Answer: $x + y = k\tan $\left(\dfrac{y - c}{k}\right)$

78769.text: If $L$ is the line with DIRECTIONS ratios $ < 3,-2,6 > $ and passing through $(1,-1,1)$, then what are the coordinates of the points on L whose distance from $(1,-1,1)$ is 2 units?
78769.sol:
Since equation of line is
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{x-1}{3}=\frac{y+1}{-2}=\frac{z-1}{6}=\lambda \text{ (let) } \\
& \Rightarrow(x, y, z)=(3 \lambda+1,-2 \lambda-1,6 \lambda+1)
\end{aligned}$
Now,
$\begin{aligned}
& \sqrt{(3 \lambda+1-1)^2+(-2 \lambda-1+1)^2+(6 \lambda+1-1)^2}=2 \\
& =\sqrt{9 \lambda^2+4 \lambda^2+36 \lambda^2}=2 \\
& \Rightarrow \sqrt{49 \lambda^2}=2 \Rightarrow \pm 7 \lambda=2 \Rightarrow \lambda= \pm \frac{2}{7}
\end{aligned}$
So, $(x, y, z)= $\$left(\frac{13}{7}, \frac{11}{7}, \frac{19}{7}\right)$or $\$left($\frac{1}{7}$, $\frac{-3}{7}$, $\frac{-5}{7}\right)$

82841.subject: Physics
82841.text:
A flask contains argon and chlorine in the ratio of $2:1$ by mass. The temperature of the mixture is $27^\circ$C. The ratio of root mean square speed of the molecules of the two gases $\left(\dfrac{v_{rms}^{Ar}}{v_{rms}^{Cl}}\right)$ is :
(Atomic mass of argon $= 40.0$ u and molecular mass of chlorine $= 70.0$ u)
82841.sol:
The root mean square speed of a gas molecule is given by $v_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$, where $T$ is the absolute temperature and $M$ is the molar mass.

For argon and chlorine in the same flask, the temperature $T$ is the same.

Therefore, the ratio of their rms speeds is inversely proportional to the square root of their molar masses:

$\dfrac{v_{rms}^{Ar}}{v_{rms}^{Cl}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{M_{Cl}}{M_{Ar}}}$

Given the molecular mass of chlorine $M_{Cl} = 70.0$ u and atomic mass of argon $M_{Ar} = 40.0$ u:

$\dfrac{v_{rms}^{Ar}}{v_{rms}^{Cl}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{70.0}{40.0}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{7}{4}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{7}}{2}$

The mass ratio of the gases in the mixture is extra information and not required for this calculation.

Answer: $\dfrac{\sqrt{7}}{2}$

84572.subject: Zoology
84572.text:
Spermatogonia undergo a series of cell divisions to produce sperms. Select the correct statements from the following :
A. Spermatogonia always undergo meiotic cell division.
B. Primary spermatocytes divide mitotically to produce secondary spermatocytes.
C. Secondary spermatocytes, through their second meiotic division, produce haploid spermatids.
D. Spermatids produce spermatozoa through mitosis.
E. Spermatids transform into spermatozoa by spermiogenesis.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
84572.sol:
Spermatogonia present on the inside wall of seminiferous tubules multiply by mitotic division and increase in numbers. Thus, statement A is incorrect.

Some of the spermatogonia called primary spermatocytes periodically undergo meiosis. A primary spermatocyte completes the first meiotic division (reduction division) leading to formation of two equal, haploid cells called secondary spermatocytes. Thus, statement B is incorrect.

The secondary spermatocytes undergo the second meiotic division to produce four equal, haploid spermatids. Thus, statement C is correct.

The spermatids are transformed into spermatozoa (sperms) by the process called spermiogenesis. No cell division (mitosis) occurs during this transformation. Thus, statement D is incorrect and statement E is correct.

Therefore, only statements C and E are correct.

Answer: C and E only

86812.subject: Physics
86812.text: Let $A$ be the mass number, $Z$ be the atomic number and $N$ be the neutron number of a nucleus. Then the statement which is always true, is
86812.sol:
The mass number $A$ is the sum of the atomic number $Z$ and the neutron number $N$, so $A = Z + N$.

Squaring both sides, we get $A^2 = (Z + N)^2 = Z^2 + N^2 + 2NZ$.

Since $Z^2 \geq 0$ and $N^2 \geq 0$, we have $Z^2 + N^2 + 2NZ \geq 2NZ$.

As $N$ and $Z$ are non-negative integers, $2NZ \geq NZ$.

Therefore, $A^2 \geq NZ$ is always true.

Checking the other options:

For $A \geq 2N \Rightarrow Z + N \geq 2N \Rightarrow Z \geq N$, which is false for heavy nuclei like $^{238}_{92}\text{U}$ where $N \gt Z$.

For $A \leq 2Z \Rightarrow Z + N \leq 2Z \Rightarrow N \leq Z$, which is also false for heavy nuclei.

For $AN \geq Z^2 \Rightarrow (Z+N)N \geq Z^2 \Rightarrow ZN + N^2 \geq Z^2$, which is false for $^{3}_{2}\text{He}$ where $Z=2, N=1$.

Answer: $A^2 \geq NZ$

89982.text: The coefficient of the term independent of $x$ in the expansion of $\left(1 + x + 2x^{3}\right){\left(\dfrac{3}{2}x^{2} - \dfrac{1}{3x}\right)}^{9}$ is
89982.sol:
Coefficient of the term independent of $x$ is the coefficient of ${x}^{0} in {\left(\dfrac{3}{2}{x}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{3x}\right)}^{9} + x{\left(\dfrac{3}{2}{x}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{3x}\right)}^{9} + 2{x}^{3}{\left(\dfrac{3}{2}{x}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{3x}\right)}^{9}$
Now, in ${\left(\dfrac{3}{2}{x}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{3x}\right)}^{9},$ ${T}_{r + 1}{=}^{9}{C}_{r}{\left(\dfrac{3}{2}{x}^{2}\right)}^{9 - r}{\left(- \dfrac{1}{3x}\right)}^{r}{=}^{9}{C}_{r}{\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)}^{9 - r}{\left(- \dfrac{1}{3}\right)}^{r}{x}^{18 - 3r}$
$\left(i\right)$ Coefficient of ${x}^{0} ⇒ 18 - 3r = 0 ⇒ r = 6$
Coefficient of ${x}^{0}$ is ${}^{9}{C}_{6}{\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)}^{3}{\left(- \dfrac{1}{3}\right)}^{6}$
$\left(ii\right)$ Coefficient of ${x}^{- 1} ⇒ 18 - 3r = - 1 ⇒ r = \dfrac{19}{3}$ (not possible)
$\left(iii\right)$ Coefficient of ${x}^{- 3} ⇒ 18 - 3r = - 3 ⇒ r = 7$
Coefficient of ${x}^{- 3}$ is ${}^{9}{C}_{7}{\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)}^{2}{\left(- \dfrac{1}{3}\right)}^{7}$
Hence, the required coefficient is
$1 \times {}^{9}{C}_{6}{\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)}^{3}{\left(- \dfrac{1}{3}\right)}^{6} + 1 \times 0 + 2 \times {}^{9}{C}_{7}{\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)}^{2}{\left(- \dfrac{1}{3}\right)}^{7}$
$= \dfrac{9 \times 8 \times 7}{3 \times 2} \times \left(\dfrac{+ 1}{8}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{27 3}\right) + 2 \times \dfrac{9 \times 8 2}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)\left(- \dfrac{1}{243 27}\right)$
$= \dfrac{7}{18} - \dfrac{2}{27} = \dfrac{17}{54}$

Given, $\dfrac{{\text{z}}_{1} - 2z{}_{2}}{2 - {\text{z}}_{1} {\overset{¯}{\text{z}}}_{2}}$  is unimodular

$⇒ \left|\dfrac{{\text{z}}_{1} - 2 {\text{z}}_{2}}{2 - {\text{z}}_{1} {\overset{¯}{\text{z}}}_{2}}\right| = 1$

$⇒ \left|{\text{z}}_{1} - 2 {\text{z}}_{2}\right| = \left|2 -  {\text{z}}_{1} {\overset{¯}{\text{z}}}_{2}\right|$

Squaring both the sides, we get,

${\left|{\text{z}}_{1} - 2z{}_{2}\right|}^{2} = {\left|2 -  {\text{z}}_{1} {\overset{¯}{\text{z}}}_{2}\right|}^{2}$

$⇒ \left({\text{z}}_{1} - 2 {\text{z}}_{2}\right) \left({\overset{¯}{\text{z}}}_{1} - 2 {\overset{¯}{\text{z}}}_{2}\right) = \left(2 - {\text{z}}_{1} {\overset{¯}{\text{z}}}_{2}\right) \left(2 - {\overset{¯}{\text{z}}}_{1} {\text{z}}_{2}\right)$

$\left(∵ {\left|\text{z}\right|}^{2} = \text{z} \overset{¯}{\text{z}}\right)$

$⇒ {\text{z}}_{1} {\overset{¯}{\text{z}}}_{1} - 2 {\text{z}}_{1} {\overset{¯}{\text{z}}}_{2} - 2 {\overset{¯}{\text{z}}}_{1} {\text{z}}_{2} + 4 {\text{z}}_{2} {\overset{¯}{\text{z}}}_{2}$

$= 4 - 2 {\overset{¯}{\text{z}}}_{1} {\text{z}}_{2} - 2 {\text{z}}_{1} {\overset{¯}{\text{z}}}_{2} + {\text{z}}_{1} {\overset{¯}{\text{z}}}_{1} {\text{z}}_{2} {\overset{¯}{\text{z}}}_{2}$

$⇒ {\left|{\text{z}}_{1}\right|}^{2} + 4 {\left|{\text{z}}_{2}\right|}^{2} = 4 + {\left|{\text{z}}_{1}\right|}^{2} {\left|{\text{z}}_{2}\right|}^{2}$

$⇒ {\left|{\text{z}}_{1}\right|}^{2} - 4 + 4 {\left|{\text{z}}_{2}\right|}^{2} - {\left|{\text{z}}_{1}\right|}^{2} {\left|{\text{z}}_{2}\right|}^{2} = 0$

$⇒ \left({\left|{\text{z}}_{1}\right|}^{2} - 4\right) \left(1 - {\left|{\text{z}}_{2}\right|}^{2}\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left|{\text{z}}_{1}\right| = 2\text{or}\left|{\text{z}}_{2}\right| = 1$

 Given, ${z}_{2}$ is not unimodular

$∴ \left|{\text{z}}_{1}\right| = 2$

91545.text: A word has $4$ identical letters and rest all are distinct letters. If the total number of words that can be made with the letters of the word be $210,$ then the total number of different letters in the word is equal to
91545.sol:
Let the number of distinct letters other than the identical letters be $n$.
Total letters $= n + 4$
Identical $= 4,$ Distinct $= n$
Number of ways in which they can be arranged $= \dfrac{\left(n + 4\right) !}{4 !}$
$⇒ \dfrac{\left(n + 4\right) !}{4 !} = 210$
$⇒ \left(n + 4\right)\left(n + 3\right)\left(n + 2\right) \ldots 6.5$
$= 210 = 7 \times 6 \times 5$
$⇒ n + 4 = 7 ⇒ n = 3$
So, the required number of total different letters $= 3 + 1 = 4$

${p}_{1} =$ probability of drawing two red balls
$= \dfrac{{}^{a}{C}_{2}}{{}^{a + b}{C}_{2}} = \dfrac{a\left(a - 1\right)}{\left(a + b\right)\left(a + b - 1\right)}$
${p}_{2} =$ probability of drawings two blue balls
$= \dfrac{{}^{b}{C}_{2}}{{}^{a + b}{C}_{2}} = \dfrac{b\left(b - 1\right)}{\left(a + b\right)\left(a + b - 1\right)}$
${p}_{3} =$ probability of drawing one red and one blue ball
$= \dfrac{{}^{a}{C}_{1}{.}^{b}{C}_{1}}{{}^{a + b}{C}_{2}} = \dfrac{2ab}{\left(a + b\right)\left(a + b - 1\right)}$
Given that ${p}_{1} = 5{p}_{2}$ and ${p}_{3} = 6{p}_{2}$
$⇔ a\left(a - 1\right) = 5b\left(b - 1\right)$ and $2ab = 6b\left(b - 1\right)$
$⇒ a = 6, b = 3 ⇒$ Total number of balls $= 9$

100242.text: A particle covers a distance from $A$ to $B$ over a period of time; the distance versus time plot is the shown below. Then which of the following is true for the motion of the particle?
options: Both average speed and instantaneous speed are always zero.
Average speed is always non-zero but instantaneous speed can be zero.
Instantaneous speed is always non-zero but average speed can be zero.
Both average speed and instantaneous speed are always non-zero.
100242.sol:
The distance versus time plot for movement of a particle from $A$ and $B$ is shown in the diagram.
From graph, it is a slope of distance-time graph for position $A$ to $C$ and $D$ to $B$ is always positive, therefore both the average speed and instantaneous speed are not always zero, therefore, option (1) is not correct. $\text{ Average velocity }=\frac{\text{ Total displacement from A to B }}{\text{ Total time interval }}$Since, total displacement depends on straight distance between initial and final points, hence, displacement between $A$ to $B$ always non zero, therefore the average speed is always non zero. Since, no distance is travelled between point $C$ to $D$ is zero. Hence, instantaneous speed at every instant between $C$ to $D$ is zero. Hence, option (2) is correct and option (3) and (4) are incorrect.
